# Instrument-air interruption during maintenance preparation

Record ID: IA-I01

At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, during Turn 2, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored. No injury is reported.

The initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment. Supporting records will be provided as the investigation develops.
spans.label: Original incident account

limitations: An incident account is not independent verification.

# Utilities area and service directory

Record ID: IA-D01 | Revision: 2 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Service areas

The Utilities air gallery serves the 1SC dryer group and distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. RHOB is the local area name used in these records; it is not an individual compressor identifier. The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.

| Location | Equipment/service | Normal record custodian |
| --- | --- | --- |
| North gallery | Site air-header connection, local indication P-U | Utilities operations |
| Dryer aisle | Dryer group D-101 and main-route valves M-101/M-102 | Utilities maintenance |
| East service rack | Auxiliary line installation area | Projects and Utilities |
| RHOB service station | Receiving header H-R and indication P-R | RHOB operations |

## Roles

Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary. RHOB operations observes the receiving process. Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release. A maintenance work order being scheduled is not a record that the boundary has been released.

This directory is a location index. It is not a current piping diagram and does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.
spans.label: IA-D01_area_and_service_directory.md

spans.text:
# Record and measurement conventions

Record ID: IA-D02 | Revision: 1 | Effective: 2024-04-01

## Measurements

Pressure values are bar gauge. A pressure tag names the measurement point, not every location on the service. The point register is needed to interpret location and scope. A running indication is not a flow measurement. A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.

## Time and identity

Wall times are local plant time on the stated date. Handwritten records are approximate unless stated otherwise. An alarm's occurrence time, acknowledgment time and export time may differ. Record aliases can persist after equipment changes; the title displayed on an alarm is not a substitute for its input mapping.

## Status conventions

“Filed” means retained in the archive. “Issued” means distributed for its stated use. “Installed” refers to a physical change. “Maintenance released” refers to work-boundary acceptance. None automatically establishes the other statuses.

An empty form field records no value. The reason it is empty requires other evidence. A draft, an issued revision and a historical reference copy can all exist at the same time.
spans.label: IA-D02_record_and_measurement_conventions.md

spans.text:
# Change and work-record requirements

Record ID: IA-D03 | Revision: 4 | Effective: 2024-03-01

## Change records

Section 3.2: When a service-routing change affects an existing maintenance boundary, the change owner identifies the affected energy-control procedure (ECP), drawing and receiving operating area. Engineering disposition is required before the changed arrangement is used for that maintenance boundary.

Section 3.4: Mechanical completion verifies the installed work covered by the completion sheet. Work-document disposition and distribution are separate signoffs. A drawing redline is not, by itself, an issued operating document.

Section 3.6: The affected ECP is either revised and issued, or an approved temporary instruction is attached to the work package. Draft preparation alone does not satisfy distribution.

## Work records

Section 5.1: The work package records the ECP revision supplied to the crew and the maintenance boundary's acceptance state. An initial notification may be entered before the event sequence has been checked.

Section 5.3: Competence and authorization records define the tasks for which a person is qualified. They do not record what that person actually observed or did on a particular job.
spans.label: IA-D03_change_and_work_record_requirements.md

| --- | --- | --- |
| P-U | Site header H-U, north gallery | Pressure upstream of the 1SC distribution routes |

# Initial desk message

Record ID: IA-C01 | Entered: 2024-05-20 10:04 | Channel: copied radio/desk note

The note is an unverified contemporaneous account.

“RHOB called air trouble. COMP FAULT on screen, acknowledged around 10:03. Might have lost the compressor again; similar call last winter. Utilities checking.”

Recorder: desk relief operator D-R. Basis recorded: screen label and radio call. The recorder was not at C-11 and did not inspect its starter or observe a trip. The note's 10:03 time is the acknowledgment time as recalled by the recorder. No compressor trip log is attached.

quotes.label: Original incident account

relationships.rationale: The maintenance preparation activity (⟦finding:c43d1e32-0eaf-42f5-bead-89202632a02d⟧) was ongoing immediately before the instrument-air pressure loss event occurred, establishing temporal precedence and situational context.
relationships.counterfactual: If no work had been in progress at that location or time, the incident might not have triggered a pause or alarm response related to operational safety during active tasks.
relationships.alternative: The pressure loss could have originated independently of any maintenance activity; however, ⟦finding:c43d1e32-0eaf-42f5-bead-89202632a02d⟧ provides context for why it was significant enough to warrant investigation and potential procedural review.
relationships.gap: No evidence directly links the preparation activity itself as a cause or contributor to the pressure loss mechanism.

relationships.rationale: The pending release of the boundary (condition) enabled the incident by allowing work to proceed without a formally verified isolation state.
relationships.counterfactual: If the maintenance boundary had been fully released and accepted prior to 10:00, the condition would have changed from 'preparation only' to 'accepted', potentially preventing reliance on an unverified configuration or triggering additional checks before proceeding with work that affected air supply.
relationships.alternative: The incident could be attributed solely to a mechanical failure of the compressor (C-11) independent of boundary status, but the lack of formal acceptance suggests procedural gaps contributed to vulnerability.
relationships.gap: Evidence does not confirm whether Utilities or RHOB operations verified valve positions independently before relying on the pending release state.

relationships.rationale: P-U monitors upstream of P-R; pressure at ⟦finding:965f70dd-56d9-430b-8f81-02150e2ea346⟧ remained normal while pressure at ⟦finding:89da63af-6894-4144-9d40-2fa88b22032f⟧ dropped.
relationships.counterfactual: If the drop had occurred before reaching H-U, both points would have shown low values simultaneously.
relationships.alternative: A leak or blockage between H-U and H-R could isolate the two readings.
relationships.gap: No direct measurement of flow or valve state in the segment between ⟦finding:965f70dd-56d9-430b-8f81-02150e2ea346⟧ and ⟦finding:89da63af-6894-4144-9d40-2fa88b22032f⟧.

relationships.rationale: The pressure drop (EVENT) triggered the alarm, which was then acknowledged as 'COMP FAULT' at ⟦finding:008e925a-e8db-41d3-9bd1-a5041e6626e0⟧.
relationships.counterfactual: If AL-44 had been updated to reflect P-R status, the label would have indicated a receiving-header fault rather than implying compressor failure.
relationships.alternative: The pressure loss could be due to distribution system issues or valve leakage upstream of RHOB, not necessarily C-11 trip.
relationships.gap: No evidence confirms whether C-11 actually tripped; the label obscures this uncertainty.

relationships.rationale: If U-A lacked authorization, the incident might have been prevented or handled differently; however, ⟦finding:983cd2ce-1af7-4242-9c8d-10bdf0cd83e4⟧ shows they were authorized. The failure to prevent relates more likely to procedural gaps (e.g., lack of change briefing) rather than qualification status itself.
relationships.counterfactual: Had U-A not held current authorization, entry into the work boundary would be prohibited by policy, potentially preventing the activity during which the air loss occurred or forcing a different response.
relationships.alternative: The pressure loss could have been caused independently of personnel qualifications (e.g., equipment failure).
relationships.gap: No evidence links U-A's specific actions to the initiation of the event; only their status is recorded.

relationships.rationale: The misconfigured mapping enabled the alarm to trigger on P-R pressure loss (supply disturbance) rather than C-11 trip, masking the true source of the interruption.
relationships.counterfactual: If AL-44 mapped to C-11's trip contact, operators would have seen a compressor-trip indication instead of COMP FAULT during supply failure, potentially prompting different troubleshooting actions earlier.
relationships.alternative: An alternative explanation is that P-R pressure loss was the sole cause regardless of mapping; however, without correct mapping, operator interpretation relies on ambiguous labels like 'COMP FAULT'.
relationships.gap: No evidence exists showing whether operators relied on C-11 trip status or assumed it based solely on COMP FAULT label during the incident.

relationships.rationale: The blank attachment (⟦finding:144e20ae-c717-4e68-a1e9-23dcf63c8758⟧) enabled the incident by failing to provide a verified record of isolation or valve positions, allowing work to proceed without confirmed boundary acceptance.
relationships.counterfactual: If WO-527-E had contained valid field execution data confirming proper isolation and valve states prior to 09:31, the crew might have recognized that maintenance was not yet ready for air-loss conditions at RHOB.
relationships.alternative: The blank attachment could represent a procedural gap rather than an equipment failure; it does not prove valves were open or closed.
relationships.gap: No evidence links the blank field directly to valve positions, only to missing documentation.
